name: Hair glue

card.summary: A bonding adhesive used to attach hair weaves, extensions and hair systems to the scalp or hair, giving instant fullness or length without sewing or braiding.
card.note: Some glues contain latex; allergic reactions including anaphylaxis have been reported.

quick.overview:
Hair glue is an adhesive used in hair-bonding to attach weaves, wefts, extensions and hair systems. It creates instant fullness, length or coverage for thinning areas without surgery.

The visible effect lasts while the bond holds and until it is removed. Hair-extension references describe glue bonding as one attachment method, alongside clips and thread, and note that use of glue has declined because of reported headaches, bald spots and dermatitis.
quick.how: A salon or wearer applies bonding glue to the wefts or hair system and attaches them near, but not directly on, the scalp. A patch test is commonly recommended before use following the manufacturer's directions, and removal uses solvents or oils.
quick.risks: Case reports describe anaphylaxis from latex in bonding glue, including one with airway compromise requiring intubation. Dermatitis, headaches and hair loss have also been linked to glue use. People with latex allergy are advised to check the ingredients.

lead: Hair glue is the adhesive used to attach hair weaves, extensions and hair systems. It lets the wearer add volume, length or coverage that blends with natural hair.

It improves how someone looks by instantly changing hair density and length. Hair-extension references say wefts can be attached with bonding glue but should not be bonded directly to the scalp, because that can cause sensitivity; glue use has declined partly because it has been linked to headaches, bald spots and dermatitis [1].

The medical literature on hair glue consists mainly of case reports of latex-related anaphylaxis [2][3] and a letter on removal with petroleum jelly [4]. A 2025 study analysed bond strength of adhesive systems on silicone facial prostheses [5].

chain: Glue bonds weave or hair system in place
angle.text: The adhesive holds added hair on the head so the look changes immediately. Bonds are temporary and need maintenance and removal.

infobox: Some products contain natural rubber latex

paras: Bonding glue is one of several ways to attach added hair. Hair-extension references list glue alongside clips and thread attachment, the latter used where bonding is unsuitable [1].

A 2002 case report described a 37-year-old woman who developed systemic anaphylaxis after repeated exposure to bonding glue, and assays found the glue contained high soluble latex antigen [2]. A 2015 emergency-medicine report described a 29-year-old woman with severe angioedema and airway compromise after a glue-applied hair weave; the latex-containing glue was removed over several hours [3]. A related letter discussed using petroleum jelly to remove hair glue [4]. Hair-extension references note patch testing and link glue to dermatitis and hair loss [1].
No controlled trials of hair glue as a cosmetic product were identified; the literature is case reports [2][3] and a bond-strength laboratory study on silicone [5].
